vignette: A 58-year-old right-handed woman has a small stroke. Her strength and sensation are normal, but when asked to show how she would use a key or brush her teeth she cannot do it with either hand, and she cannot copy meaningless hand postures. She understands the instructions and can describe the actions in words.
explanation: Ideomotor apraxia of both hands with intact comprehension and strength is a lesion of the dominant left inferior parietal lobule, which stores the movement formulas that the right hemisphere receives through the corpus callosum; a callosal lesion would spare the right hand, and a right parietal lesion would produce neglect rather than apraxia.
